subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should OpenClaw promote the existing late-success count repair into a general compaction-completion reconciliation boundary, and which session fields should that boundary own?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing the authoritative boundary and enrolled session fields affects persisted session semantics, status surfaces, auth-profile rotation, and memory-flush behavior.

options.title: Design bounded reconciliation boundary
options.body: Promote the existing count repair into one owner-approved helper or event and enroll only fields with clear compaction-completion semantics and idempotent update rules.

options.title: Keep local symptom fixes
options.body: Leave the current count repair in place and handle status, metadata timestamps, and diagnostics through separate narrower PRs as symptoms appear.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Defer architecture work until a concrete current-main user-visible mismatch proves which additional state must converge.

recommendation.title: Design bounded reconciliation boundary
recommendation.body: Promote the existing count repair into one owner-approved helper or event and enroll only fields with clear compaction-completion semantics and idempotent update rules.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman reviewed the original narrow reconciliation fix and is the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether that boundary should generalize.
